mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, which positively impacts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 forward returns higher over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 9% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate exceeds 9% but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the next 20 trading days, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month and the federal funds rate is above 4%, it indicates tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both CPI increases by >0.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4%, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If payroll employment increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the next 5 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases by more than 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real disposable personal income suggests higher consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If real disposable income increases by more than 1% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is above 8% and payroll employment growth is below 100,000, it signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase by more than 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, the hypothesis is falsified.
